Back in July, Apple rolled out an update adding basic search functionality to its TestFlight app. While you might think such a simple update would be universally welcomed, the same version of TestFlight introduced a rather annoying bug for many users.

Personally, I wasn't significantly impacted by this bug. Because of that, I considered the TestFlight update at the time to be a simple yet meaningful improvement.

Sometimes, even small changes can have an outsized impact. That's especially true for the latest TestFlight update from Apple for users with large libraries of pre-release software. Apple just pushed out an update to TestFlight for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and more. The new version, 4.3, includes a "search field for quickly finding apps."

In hindsight, I did notice some strange things, which I flagged at the end of the story (though I had it exactly backwards):

I think the reason I missed the bug is that last year I preserved multiple years of TestFlight records for apps as part of "merging" my formerly separate iCloud and App Store Apple accounts. It was a pain to request, but worth it for me.

Regardless, the TestFlight app bug did not escape the notice of John Vorhees at MacStories:

So, you can imagine my excitement when I read Zac Hall's piece at 9to5Mac about TestFlight finally adding a search field. "Finally!" I thought. I immediately dropped what I was doing and updated the app. […] However, there is a very large "but" to this story. I rather liked the way TestFlight betas were previously arranged in reverse chronological order. […] Now, however, the expired betas have been scattered among the alphabetically sorted active TestFlight betas, and the list of expired betas appears to have expanded to include every beta I have ever been a part of. I counted roughly 800 app entries for me. You can imagine how few of those are active betas. The search helps, but it's no longer browsable by scrolling.

In August, John Gruber wrote about the TestFlight update and bug at Daring Fireball:

Last night, more than a month after the bug was introduced (and flagged by Vorhees), Apple finally updated TestFlight for the first time. The release notes mention only bug fixes, but the update does address the bug.

TestFlight 4.3.1 is the fix for users affected by this regression.
